Balanced
A solid all-rounder with no clear weaknesses, but also no specialist bonus.
No adjustment risks and a stable effect in all areas.
No particular strength in crises, youth development, tactics or finances.
Motivator
Strong in crises, close matches and after setbacks.
Better morale and a stronger comeback effect.
Less tactical precision and not always the board’s favourite choice.
Tactician
Gets more from a suitable playing philosophy and a stable formation.
Small advantages in passing, match planning and tactical fit.
Less emotional lift; fans sometimes react more cautiously.
Disciplinarian
Brings order, fitness and fewer unnecessary risks.
Lower card risk and better training discipline.
Player satisfaction and enthusiasm may suffer.
Talent developer
Ideal for youth, young players and long-term squad building.
Better youth development and training effects for young players.
Less short-term impact in high-pressure matches and with older stars.
Media expert
Can manage pressure better and make better use of interviews.
Media pressure rises more slowly and interview effects are more favourable.
The board and dressing room sometimes view this style as too soft.
Financial strategist
Thinks economically and improves perceptions of financial stability.
The board responds better to transfers, objectives and stable finances.
Fans react more sensitively to sales and a lack of sporting ambition.
Club icon
Lives for the club and enjoys greater support from the fans.
Stronger fan loyalty, home advantage and derby effect.
Unpopular sales and unfamiliar environments are more difficult.
Risk taker
Brave, attacking and capable of surprises.
Greater upside with an attacking approach and positive events.
More volatility, higher pressure and a greater penalty for failure.
